cf.title: Add recovery boundary WAL record for database and tablespace commands

input.subject: [PATCH] Add recovery boundary WAL record for database and tablespace commands

verdict_reasoning: The goal has shown demand and no objection at level 1 survived. The design does not yet meet its own aim: replication-ondisk-1 shows a time target between the boundary record and the commit still leaves a broken cluster, and standards-compat-1 shows recovery_target_inclusive changes the result at an equal timestamp. The list needs to agree whether a narrowed window is acceptable before code review. maintenance-fit-1 is a smaller design point.

brief.title: Recovery boundary WAL record for database and tablespace commands
brief.problem: recovery_target_time is checked only on commit and abort records, so a time target set before CREATE/DROP DATABASE, ALTER DATABASE SET TABLESPACE or CREATE/DROP TABLESPACE does not stop recovery before their file operations. After PITR the cluster has a catalog entry with no directory, or an orphan directory. Delayed standbys also apply these file operations at once, ignoring recovery_min_apply_delay.
brief.proposed_design: 0001 writes a new XLOG2 record with a timestamp before the first irreversible record of each of the five commands, and recoveryStopsBefore() stops before it when the timestamp is past a recovery_target_time target. The record has no redo action and does not affect other target types. 0002 makes recovery_min_apply_delay also wait on this record.
user_visible_surface: New XLOG2 WAL record type RECOVERY_BOUNDARY with a timestamp, shown by pg_waldump; XLOG_PAGE_MAGIC is bumped.
New log message "recovery stopping before recovery boundary, time ...".
recovery_target_time can now stop recovery before these five commands, not only at commit or abort.
recovery_min_apply_delay now also delays the file operations of these commands; the config.sgml paragraph changes.
author_claims: Stopping before the boundary record loses nothing, because replaying the record has no effect.
The bug was reported twice before, in 2019 (loxodata) and later (pgbackrest).
xid and LSN targets with inclusive = off show the same result on master; the author treats that as a separate, documented behaviour.
v2 is only a rebase of v1.
brief.thread_state: Shihao Zhong asked about xid targets; the author declined to cover them. João Rito tested v2 and confirmed the fix, but reported that targets between the boundary and the commit still break the database, an inclusive = on equality edge case, and missing docs in 0001; the author has not replied.
unclear: How the patch handles a time target that falls between the boundary record and the commit, which João Rito showed still leaves a broken database.
Whether the comparison should be >= for both recovery_target_inclusive settings.
Why 0001 does not document the new stop behaviour or the xid and LSN limits.
Whether the boundary record should name the command it belongs to.
Why decode.c is touched and what logical decoding does with the new record.
Whether this is meant for back-patching, given the Bugfix tag and the XLOG_PAGE_MAGIC bump.
search_queries: new WAL record timestamp recovery target

prior_attempts.title: PITR enhance getRecordTimestamp()
prior_attempts.what_is_different: The row's title suggests it changed getRecordTimestamp() so recovery could read times from more existing records. This proposal adds a new timestamped record for five database and tablespace commands. The row records no reason for the withdrawal.

objections.title: Boundary record leaves a window where PITR still breaks the catalog
objections.failure_scenario: An operator sets recovery_target_time to a moment while DROP DATABASE or CREATE DATABASE was waiting on its checkpoints. Recovery passes the boundary record, replays the file operation, then stops before the commit. After promotion the operator finds a database that cannot be connected to, or an orphan base/<oid>.
objections.argument: The invariant the patch aims for is that the catalog and the directories agree after a time-targeted PITR. Message #4 shows this still fails for any target between the boundary and the commit, and these commands wait on checkpoints in that span. The proposal only narrows the window and does not say so. The author has not replied, and message #4 also found an inclusive = on equality case where the comparison lets the file operation through.
objections.author_must_show: Is a partial fix acceptable for the window between boundary and commit, and if so, how will operators learn which targets remain unsafe?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 reproduced a broken cluster for targets between the boundary record and the commit, with a window of about one second for CREATE DATABASE. The proposal does not state this limit, and the author has not answered.

objections.title: Inclusive and exclusive time targets give different results at the boundary
objections.failure_scenario: An operator sets recovery_target_time to a time recorded just before a DROP DATABASE and leaves recovery_target_inclusive = on. Recovery replays the directory removal and stops before the commit, and connecting fails with "cannot connect to invalid database". The same target with inclusive = off leaves a clean cluster.
objections.argument: 0001 reuses the commit-record comparison for a record that is not a transaction and cannot be "included", so recovery_target_inclusive has no clear meaning for it. Message #4 shows the two settings giving different results for the same WAL and suggests >= for both. 0001 adds no documentation of the new stop point, and the author has not replied to message #4.
objections.author_must_show: What should recovery_target_inclusive mean for a boundary record, and where do the recovery_target_time docs state the new stop point and its limits?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 shows inclusive = on and off give different results when the target equals the boundary time, and the author has not replied. The scenario should say "exactly equal": targets just before the command were clean for both settings.

objections.title: Every future file-operating DDL path must remember the boundary record
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a new CREATE DATABASE strategy or a new directory operation in dbcommands.c or tablespace.c without emitting the boundary record first. No test or assertion fails. Operators find out after a PITR to a time target leaves an orphan or missing directory, the same bug this patch fixes.
objections.argument: The fix relies on placing a call before "the first irreversible record" at each of five call sites in two files. Nothing in recovery checks that a non-transactional file record follows a boundary record. The new tests in 003_recovery_targets.pl cover only today's five commands, so a reviewer of a later patch is likely to miss the requirement.
objections.author_must_show: What makes a future file-operating record without a preceding boundary record fail loudly, for example an assertion or a check during replay?

critic.reasoning: The fix depends on a call placed by hand at five sites, and the material shows no replay check or assertion that catches a missing one. A missed site only returns to today's behaviour and such commands are rare, so fixable is the right severity.

refuted.title: Bugfix tag conflicts with a WAL format change that cannot be back-patched
refuted.failure_scenario: A user on a supported release hits the reported PITR bug and waits for a minor release. The fix needs a new XLOG2 record and an XLOG_PAGE_MAGIC bump, so it cannot appear in a minor release. If back-patched anyway, a standby still on the older minor release would stop replay on the unknown record.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix and targets version 20, while the commit message bumps XLOG_PAGE_MAGIC. The bug was first reported in 2019 (message #1), so most affected users run branches this design cannot reach. A committer would likely ask what supported branches get, such as a documentation warning for recovery_target_time.
refuted.author_must_show: Is this meant for master only, and if so, what do supported branches get for the same bug, such as a documented warning?

critic.reasoning: The CommitFest entry targets version 20 and nobody in the thread proposes a back-patch, so the mixed minor release scenario does not arise. Back branches keeping an existing bug is the state today and is not a flaw in this design.

refuted.title: New WAL record and page magic bump conflict with the Bugfix tag
refuted.failure_scenario: If this is back-patched and a primary gets the new minor release before its standbys, the primary writes RECOVERY_BOUNDARY records that the older standbys cannot decode. Replay on those standbys stops with an error at the first CREATE or DROP DATABASE. If it is not back-patched, every supported branch keeps the bug.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix, but 0001 adds a new XLOG2 record type and bumps XLOG_PAGE_MAGIC. A committer would likely treat that as master-only. The proposal does not say whether back branches get the fix, or what they get instead, such as a documentation note. The bug has been reported twice over several years, so the back-branch answer matters to the users who reported it.
refuted.author_must_show: Is the fix meant for master only, and if so, what do supported branches get for the reported PITR breakage?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which is refuted because the entry targets version 20 and no back-patch is proposed.

refuted.title: Permanent WAL record type for a fix that leaves part of the window open
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator picks a recovery_target_time while DROP DATABASE or CREATE DATABASE is still waiting for its checkpoints. Recovery passes the boundary record and stops before the commit, and the cluster again has a catalog row with no directory or an orphan base/<oid>. The project still has to support the new record type in pg_waldump, decoding and every future WAL reader.
refuted.argument: Message #4 shows this window with real timings: about one second for CREATE DATABASE file_copy, and also at boundary time plus one microsecond for DROP DATABASE. The boundary timestamp is taken at command start, while the commit comes after checkpoint waits. Message #4 also reports that inclusive = on with an exactly equal target gives a broken result. The author has not replied, so it is open whether the record is the right long-term shape or a stopgap that later stays in the WAL format.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is a separate timestamp-only record better long term than a design that also closes the boundary-to-commit window, such as checking the target on the file-operation records themselves?

critic.reasoning: WAL is not carried across major versions, so a later major release can remove the record type, and the suggested check on file-operation records would still replay them for a target inside the window. The window itself is a duplicate of replication-ondisk-1.

refuted.title: Bugfix tag conflicts with a new WAL record and XLOG_PAGE_MAGIC bump
refuted.failure_scenario: If this goes into minor releases, a primary updated before its standby writes RECOVERY_BOUNDARY records, and the older standby stops replay on an unknown record type. If it does not, users on all supported branches keep hitting the PITR bug and get no fix.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix but targets version 20, and the commit message bumps XLOG_PAGE_MAGIC. The reports in message #1 are years old and affect released branches. The proposal does not say whether back branches get this fix, a different fix, or a documentation note only.
refuted.author_must_show: Is this intended for back branches, and if so, how do standbys on an older minor release handle the new record?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which is refuted because the entry targets version 20 and no back-patch is proposed.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: 0001 bumps XLOG_PAGE_MAGIC and touches pg_control.h, so the WAL format on disk changes.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: 0001 adds the XLOG2 RECOVERY_BOUNDARY record and a new stop point; 0002 changes what a delayed standby waits on.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry is tagged Bugfix, but the new record type and XLOG_PAGE_MAGIC bump limit it to version 20.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Five call sites in dbcommands.c and tablespace.c must each write the boundary record, and future file-operating commands must do the same.

questions: Is a partial fix intended for time targets between the boundary record and the commit, and if so, how do operators learn which targets remain unsafe?
What should recovery_target_inclusive mean for a boundary record, and should the comparison be >= for both settings as message #4 suggests?
What makes a future file-operating WAL record without a preceding boundary record fail loudly, for example an assertion or a check during replay?

committability.owner_note: Needs a committer who knows the recovery target and replay delay code in xlogrecovery.c and the WAL logging of database and tablespace commands.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a new WAL record type, a new recovery stop point and a changed recovery_min_apply_delay rule. PITR results that still break inside the boundary-to-commit window would be reported against this commit.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered message #2 within a day and posted a rebase. The author has not yet replied to message #4.

priority.reason: Two field reports and a tester's reproduction show real demand among users of time-targeted PITR and delayed standbys. The patch is small, but it touches recovery stop logic, and the window and recovery_target_inclusive questions from message #4 are open.

provisional_note: The code was not read. The handling of the new record in decode.c, the exact placement of the boundary record at each call site, and the interaction of the two waits in 0002 could not be judged.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve recovery performance of dropping database having many tablespaces
precedents_retrieved.summary: DROP DATABASE would write one XLOG_DBASE_DROP record listing all tablespaces of the database, instead of one record per tablespace. On a standby, replay would then scan shared_buffers once, not once per tablespace.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers supported the idea and found the patch logically correct, but asked for performance numbers that show the recovery gain. One tester saw no difference with the patch, and Simon Riggs asked to rename tablespace_num to ntablespaces. The author did not respond for about two and a half months while the patch waited on author, so Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This was a couple of months ago, and nothing has happened since with the
patch waiting on author, so the patch is marked as returned with
feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add force flag while doing pg_restore to force dropping database in case of existing connections
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a --force option to pg_restore so that, with --create and --clean, it drops the target database with DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE) and disconnects existing sessions. The patch rewrites the stored drop statement for the database entry and checks that the server version supports WITH (FORCE).
precedents_retrieved.objection: Daniel Gustafsson argued that the name --force suggests the restore will succeed regardless of state, but WITH (FORCE) still fails in common cases such as dropping the currently open database, so users would be confused. He also found that the --help output was updated for pg_dump instead of pg_restore and that the patch raised a compiler warning. Peter Eisentraut noted disagreement on whether the option was wanted, and the entry was returned because these comments were not addressed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think
the risk for user confusion outweighs the benefits, or maybe I'm just not smart
enough to see all the benefits?

precedents_retrieved.title: New argument "latest" for recovery_target parameter
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a value "latest" for recovery_target that makes recovery apply all available WAL explicitly, so recovery_target_action takes effect and backup tools can detect conflicting targets. Later versions also defined end of WAL for standbys by changing WaitForWALToBecomeAvailable to return when the archive, pg_wal and streaming sources were exhausted.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tomas Vondra returned the patch because it had been waiting on the author with no update since early December, after Kyotaro Horiguchi's review of the 2019-12-08 version. Peter Eisentraut supported making the existing default behavior explicit, but said a new end-of-WAL behavior for standbys needed a separate discussion, and he disliked the name "latest".

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow PostgreSQL to perform promote/pause/shutdown operations at end-of-the-wal when the recovery does not reach the recovery target
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal stops recovery from promoting at the end of available WAL when the recovery target was not reached, with a new setting (recovery_target_incomplete) to promote, pause or shut down instead. It later split into a second patch that refuses to start WAL replay when the recovery target lies before the restored backup's position, checked against pg_control.
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Steele found the start-point check incorrect: it uses the checkpoint in pg_control, but backup recovery starts from the backup_label checkpoint, and PITR can only start at backup end. The check would accept invalid targets in long backups and reject valid ones, and the last completed xid says little about commit order. He also noted that no consensus existed for the behaviour change, and returned the patch at the end of the CF.

My point is that the
information you are working from (whatever checkpoint happens to be in
pg_control when recovery starts) is not sufficient for the task.  This

precedents_retrieved.title: Reduce the time required for a database recovery from archive.
precedents_retrieved.authors: Anna Akenteva (a.akenteva), Dmitry Shulga (d.shulga), Ivan Taranov (i.taranov)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add background workers that run restore_command in parallel to prefetch archived WAL segments into pg_wal/pgsql_tmp, so the startup process finds the next segment ready during recovery. A new GUC max_restore_command_workers sets the number of workers, and a compiled-in multiplier of 16 sets how many segments are prefetched.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Stephen Frost objected that the user can tune the prefetch amount only through max_restore_command_workers, and asked for a separate setting for the amount of WAL to prefetch. He also noted that with 1 GiB WAL segments the fixed multiplier needs 16 GiB of space before any prefetching happens. He questioned why the startup process has to hand each file to a worker. The author did not answer his last review, the entry stayed Waiting on Author, and it was returned with feedback when the commitfest closed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Ah, it wasn't mentioned that we've got a multiplier in here, but it still ends up meaning that if a user actually wants to tune the amount of pre-fetching being done, they're going to end up having to tune the, pretty much entirely unrelated, value of max_restore_command_workers.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reduce the time required for a database recovery from archive.
precedents_retrieved.authors: Anna Akenteva (a.akenteva), Dmitry Shulga (d.shulga), Ivan Taranov (i.taranov)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch made archive recovery faster by having background workers run restore_command in parallel, so they fetch upcoming WAL segments into pg_wal/pgsql_tmp before the startup process needs them. A later version replaced max_restore_command_workers with wal_prefetch_workers and a wal_max_prefetch_amount limit on how many files are fetched ahead.
precedents_retrieved.objection: In March 2021 the patch no longer applied and the entry went to Waiting on Author. David Steele objected to the design: Postgres should ask restore_command for a batch of WAL that backup tools can fetch in parallel, and workers that request WAL without knowing what exists can flood the archive with requests for missing files. Andrey Borodin supported redesigning restore_command and archive_command. The visible messages end in March 2021 and do not show the October 2021 closing message.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Several third-party backup solutions support parallel archive get so it would be nice to support an interface that simply says to the restore_command, "go get 1gb of WAL and write the files here.

precedents_retrieved.title: I thought it would be better to add a POSIx_fadvise description for the recovery_prefetch parameter here, to distinguish it from the database functions.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The entry proposes adding a description of posix_fadvise to the documentation of the recovery_prefetch parameter, to set it apart from database functions. It is attached to the WAL prefetch thread, where recovery reads ahead in the WAL and calls PrefetchBuffer() for referenced blocks, which relies on POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. None of the shown messages discusses the documentation change. The last messages cover a buildfarm failure on topminnow, which Thomas Munro traced to pg_walinspect rather than to the prefetch code.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert recent changes related to handling of 2PC files at recovery
precedents_retrieved.authors: Michael Paquier, Alexander Korotkov, Simon Riggs
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert recent changes related to handling of 2PC files at recovery
Reverted commit(s): Fix handling of orphaned 2PC files in the future at recovery; Fix failures with incorrect epoch handling for 2PC files at recovery; Make use FullTransactionId in 2PC filenames; Speedup 2PC recovery by skipping two phase state files in normal path
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts 8f67f994e8ea (down to v13) and c3de0f9eed38 (down to
v17), as these are proving to not be completely correct regarding two
aspects:
- In v17 and newer branches, c3de0f9eed38's check for epoch handling is
incorrect, and does not correctly handle frozen epochs.  A logic closer
to widen_snapshot_xid() should be used.  The 2PC code should try to
integrate deeper with FullTransactionIds, 5a1dfde8334b being not enough.
- In v13 and newer branches, 8f67f994e8ea is a workaround for the real
issue, which is that we should not attempt CLOG lookups without reaching
consistency.  This exists since 728bd991c3c4, and this is reachable with
ProcessTwoPhaseBuffer() called by restoreTwoPhaseData() at the beginning
of recovery.

Per discussion with Noah Misch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Reduce checkpoints and WAL traffic on low activity database server"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Reduce checkpoints and WAL traffic on low activity database server"
Reverted commit(s): Reduce checkpoints and WAL traffic on low activity database server Previously, we skipped a checkpoint if no WAL had been written since last checkpoint, though this does not appear in user documentation. As of now, we skip a checkpoint until we have written at least one enough WAL to switch the next WAL file. This greatly reduces the level of activity and number of WAL messages generated by a very low activity server. This is safe because the purpose of a checkpoint is to act as a starting place for a recovery, in case of crash. This patch maintains minimal WAL volume for replay in case of crash, thus maintaining very low crash recovery time.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 18fb9d8d21a28caddb72c7ffbdd7b96d52ff9724.  Per
discussion, it does not seem like a good idea to allow committed changes to
go un-checkpointed indefinitely, as could happen in a low-traffic server;
that makes us entirely reliant on the WAL stream with no redundancy that
might aid data recovery in case of disk failure.

This re-introduces the original problem of hot-standby setups generating a
small continuing stream of WAL traffic even when idle, but there are other
ways to address that without compromising crash recovery, so we'll revisit
that issue in a future release cycle.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert pg_wal_replay_wait() stored procedure
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert pg_wal_replay_wait() stored procedure
Reverted commit(s): Implement pg_wal_replay_wait() stored procedure; pg_wal_replay_wait(): Fix typo in the doc; Adjust pg_wal_replay_wait() procedure behavior on promoted standby; Improve header comment for WaitLSNSetLatches(); Add tests for pg_wal_replay_wait() errors
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts 3c5db1d6b0, and subsequent improvements and fixes
including 8036d73ae3, 867d396ccd, 3ac3ec580c, 0868d7ae70, 85b98b8d5a,
2520226c95, 014f9f34d2, e658038772, e1555645d7, 5035172e4a, 6cfebfe88b,
73da6b8d1b, and e546989a26.

The reason for reverting is a set of remaining issues.  Most notably, the
stored procedure appears to need more effort than the utility statement
to turn the backend into a "snapshot-less" state.  This makes an approach
to use stored procedures questionable.

Catversion is bumped.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent records a reason that applies here. [P15] is the closest match but records no reason for its withdrawal. [P12] reverted a fix for replaying create database records on a standby, and its recorded reason concerns that specific approach. Message #1 cites two earlier reports of the bug, and message #2 says both have been open for years. Those are bug reports, not rejected fixes, so they support demand and give no grounds for rejection.
Other contract points look settled. The xid and LSN behaviour is the existing documented behaviour (message #3), and 0002 updates the recovery_min_apply_delay docs for its behaviour change.
Logical decoding of the new record (decode.c) and the double wait in 0002 could not be judged without the code. Neither yields a concrete failure scenario from the material.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. The boundary record is written only by commands that already need CREATEDB, ownership or superuser, and adds no new data beyond a timestamp. recovery_target_time and recovery_min_apply_delay stay superuser-set, and 0002's delay matches the per-commit delay any user can already cause, so it adds no new denial-of-service path.
Hot-path cost looks negligible because the record is written only by rare DDL. No new GUC, catalog or external dependency is involved.

No existing feature does this job. An operator can find the LSN of the first database or tablespace record with pg_waldump and recover with recovery_target_lsn, but only after learning that a time target silently produced a broken cluster, and no extension can add a timestamped WAL record to these commands. A committer is unlikely to call this a duplicate, because the record would give recovery its only timestamp before these file operations.

Demand is shown. Two independent field reports, from 2019 and later, are cited in message #1, and message #2 notes both stayed open for years. In message #4 a tester reproduced a missing database directory and orphan directories after PITR on master. A delayed standby that removes a dropped database's directory at once defeats the usual reason to run one, so 0002 also has a clear user group. The cost falls mostly on the five database and tablespace commands and on recovery_target_time users.
